compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Two people might both ask for a decision and agree that the same standard should apply to everyone. That is compatible with shared T and J. The same behavior could also come from their responsibilities or a tight deadline.

### ESTJ and INTJ: setting rules for a customer community

In this fictional example, a private customer community has 3,000 members across eight channels. Some members post competitor links, others post daily ads, and some visit only during promotions. Two support staff review the same posts and moderation logs, have the same authority, and have one week to propose changes.

One way to assess the problem is to review comparable cases: what was posted, how moderators applied the rule, and where enforcement broke down. That illustrates Sensing, particularly the use of precedent in Si. Past cases are a useful guide when the situations are comparable, but they may miss a new kind of post.

Another way is to look across those same posts and records for a pattern: does the community mainly serve support requests, repeat customers, or referrals? compare_blocks.body:
The following fictional examples illustrate how people can weigh the same information differently. Assign work or evaluate performance using responsibilities, relevant experience, and evidence from the job.

### ESTJ and INTJ: a new platform rule changes the problem

In this fictional example, customers say useful posts are getting buried. Two moderators with the same authority receive the same update: starting next month, the platform will hide external links by default and log them, and three major customers say their product previews have been removed as ads.

The complaint narrows the question: how should moderators distinguish previews from ads? One proposal uses specific false positives to define eligibility, review, and appeals. A detailed rule can be hard to maintain. Another uses patterns in recent posts and customer feedback to test whether frequent buyers and casual members need different channels. Any new structure still needs rules moderators can apply. Either person can propose both, and neither approach identifies their type.

The two proposals can be combined. To test the moderation plan, count inquiries, complaints, ads, and general conversation using the same definitions before and after a two-week trial. Check a specific prediction: the share of ads will fall without a drop in legitimate inquiries. This measures the effects of the trial, not the moderators’ personalities.

### ESTJ and INTJ: responding to health claims in a family chat

In this fictional family chat, a relative regularly shares wellness articles and several family members buy the products they recommend. Family members can distinguish a claim’s traceable source from evidence that supports it. Questions about someone’s condition, medication, or treatment belong with a qualified health professional.

The family wants to flag an unverified claim and keep the conversation respectful. One approach looks at the group’s existing rules and who can clarify them. Both types can speak up in the group or check in privately. Neither response shows how much someone respects their relatives or what type they are.
